title: P0 native tool capability system: registry, unified runtime, model-driven tool loop and tool lifecycle
user_story: As an AI research agent I discover, select, chain and recover from tools myself inside an environment that enforces authorization, budgets and provenance, so research actions are agent-driven yet traceable and reproducible.

requirements.description: Central versioned registry over builtin, manifest and external MCP tools with schema-validated specs, capability/lexical search, lazy full specifications, runtime availability detection, version constraints/active pointer and app compatibility.

One execution interface for native, python, cli, mcp and container tools: async jobs, streamed observations, timeout and cancellation, structured errors, bounded retry only for retryable idempotent failures, input/output schema validation.

Authority only from a Grant (tool patterns, permissions, mutation, expiry, call/time/output budgets); models, specs, manifests and tool output cannot widen it; manifests cannot be native, reuse builtin ids or inject host paths/interpreters.

Every call including denied/invalid/failed appends a hash-chained provenance record bound to principal, grant, exact tool version and spec digest, argument/result digests and attempts; tampering is detected; succeeded calls can be replayed and compared.

Model-driven loop with no tool-specific logic or keyword forcing: agent-initiated discovery (including tools added mid-task), selection, multi-tool composition, recovery and switching from structured errors; execution claims must cite succeeded jobs.
Session tool_mode=agent replaces keyword pre-selection in chat; authority stays the session MCP allowlist (topic isolation keeps none), read-only and bounded; default legacy behavior unchanged.

Agents can propose tools into an isolated proposal area; validation runs declared examples through the runtime (agent-written python inside a no-network container, host only by explicit owner setting), binds to the proposal digest; promotion needs a named non-agent approver; versions immutable; rollback re-points the active version.
Additive /api/tools HTTP routes for discovery, describe, invoke, jobs/events/stream/cancel, provenance/verify, MCP servers and proposal lifecycle with structured error status codes.

Optional, default-off Google Colab (official googlecolab/colab-mcp local stdio bridge) and Google Drive (official remote drivemcp.googleapis.com) MCP tools confined to a dedicated per-project folder: isolated local folder/HOME/caches/temp and credential-free environment for the Colab process with only that folder advertised as MCP root; Drive FolderGuard default-deny (containment proof for reads/downloads/copies, forced parent for create/copy, filtered search, unknown tools withheld, fail closed on unverifiable shapes); OAuth PKCE token stored in the isolated folder and sent only to *.googleapis.com by application-defined specs.

External agent clients (e.g. Antigravity used directly by the researcher as an MCP client, Codex, Claude Code) reach the registry through /mcp meta-tools search/describe/call; ephemeral session grants keep their allowlist; direct clients get owner-configured tools.mcp_permissions without mutation; per-session budget; meta-tools cannot recurse; owner switch tools.mcp_registry.

nonfunctional: No new runtime dependency; JSON Schema subset rejects unsupported keywords instead of silently ignoring them

Process tools run with allowlisted environment (no provider/GitHub credentials), python -I, no shell, private working directory and whole-tree kill; containers read-only, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, pids/memory/cpu limits, no network unless granted; defense in depth, not certified OS sandbox
Existing /mcp, mission capabilities and API/SSE contracts unchanged; new routes additive
Bounded: per-grant calls/time/output, per-tool timeout/output, loop max steps, observation truncation
inputs: Tool manifests and builtin MCP tool declarations
postconditions: No tool runs without an authorizing grant
dependencies: Optional: uv/uvx + network for googlecolab/colab-mcp; Google OAuth Web client and Workspace Developer Preview for Drive MCP
acceptance_criteria: Agent discovers a tool installed after the task started and uses it (MOCKED model, real registry/runtime)
Agent selects without hardcoding: loop source has no tool names/keyword routing; chat agent mode never calls keyword propose
Agent composes tools, recovers from invalid input and execution failure, switches tools
Real local model executes a real numerical experiment with independently recomputed measurements (separate LIVE_PROVIDER acceptance, not mandatory CI)
Denied, expired, over-budget and non-granted calls are refused and recorded
Provenance chain verifies; tampering detected; replay reproduces deterministic results

recovery: Feature is additive and default-off for chat (tool_mode=legacy). Disable by keeping legacy mode; registry data lives only in project data/tools and tool_runs. Max three repair cycles under TASK-NATIVE-TOOLS-660.
test_environment: REAL_LOCAL subprocesses, loopback MCP HTTP server, FastAPI TestClient and files in disposable PHDLAB_DATA_DIR; agent-loop and chat cases use an explicitly MOCKED scripted model; container execution MOCKED at the process boundary; real-model acceptance separately in tools/tool_agent_acceptance.py (LIVE_PROVIDER). Google: real stdio fixture process and loopback HTTP fixture standing in for Google servers; Google OAuth token endpoint MOCKED; live Google compatibility recorded separately.

review.method: Same-agent adversarial review (not independent): authority sources, manifest injection paths, process/containment, provenance integrity, keyword-forcing removal scope. Fixed during review: builtin id override, manifest home/python injection, MCP snapshot kind confusion.
